newsitem.title: USA: US CREDIT OUTLOOK -- Weary mkt eys Claims, Phila Fed.
newsitem.headline: US CREDIT OUTLOOK -- Weary mkt eys Claims, Phila Fed.

text.p: Economic news returns to center stage Thursday, which players see as the last day before the tired U.S. Treasury market virtually shuts down until after the new year.
A trio of economic releases are due throughout the morning. At 0830 EST/1330 the Labor Department reports weekly jobless claims figures, while Commerce puts out its latest trade data.
At 1000 EST/1500 GMT, the Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia's December business outlook survey is due.

Players said that the bull market reamins, despite backing up considerably the past month or so. Rather, they said, the market is concerned that the economy is growing fast enough that the Fed may have to tighten sometime in 1997.

In late trade Wednesday, the when-issued five-year note was at 6.23 percent. The 30-year bond was at 97-13/32, down 15/32, to yield 6.70 percent -- its highest level since closing at 6.71 percent October 30. The 10-year note was 11/32 lower at 100-7/32 to yield 6.47 percent.
